A B C♯ D E F♯ G♯ A
A B♭ C D E F G A
A B C D E F G A
questions.why: A harmonic minor scale raises the 7th degree. On A that gives A B C D E F G♯ A, with G♯ instead of G.

questions.q: After C, G, D, A on the circle of fifths comes…
questions.why: The circle of fifths adds a sharp each step up a fifth: C (0), G (1), D (2), A (3), then E (4 sharps).

questions.q: Why does F major use B♭ and not A♯?
options: Each letter appears once in a scale
questions.why: A scale uses each letter name once, so F major uses B♭ rather than A♯. A♯ would repeat A and leave out B.

questions.q: In 6/8, how many dotted-quarter beats per bar?
questions.why: 6/8 has six eighth notes grouped in two sets of three, so there are two dotted-quarter beats per bar.

courses.title: Starter paths: guitar, keyboard, tabla and bansuri
courses.summary: Pick up a first instrument the right way: posture, first sounds, first songs and a practice path for guitar, keyboard, tabla and bansuri flute.
outcomes: Learners can tune and play 5 open chords on guitar
Learners can play a C major scale with correct fingering on keyboard
Learners can produce basic tabla bols and play keherwa theka
Learners can make a clear tone on bansuri and play Sa Re Ga
Learners can follow a structured daily practice routine

lessons.title: Guitar: tuning, first chords and strumming

scenes.text: Neel, 15, in Dehradun, gets a second-hand acoustic guitar. His fingers hurt and the chords buzz.
His neighbour Ms. Kapoor fixes three things in one afternoon: tuning, thumb position and pressing just behind the fret.
She gives him a 15-minute daily plan: chord changes, strumming, one song.
In three weeks, the buzzing is gone and the soreness has turned into calluses.

steps.title: Strings and tuning
steps.body: Standard tuning, from the **thickest (6th)** string to the **thinnest (1st)**: **E A D G B E**. Remember it as 'Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie'. Use a clip-on tuner or a free tuner app. Tune **up** to the note (if you're above it, go below and come back up) — the string tends to hold its pitch better.

steps.title: Five open chords to start
steps.body:
- **Em** – 2nd fret A string and 2nd fret D string; strum all 6.
- **Am** – 1st fret B, 2nd fret D, 2nd fret G; strum from the A string (5 strings).
- **C** – 3rd fret A, 2nd fret D, 1st fret B; strum from the A string.
- **G** – 3rd fret low E, 2nd fret A, 3rd fret high E; strum all 6.
- **D** – 2nd fret G, 3rd fret B, 2nd fret high E; strum from the D string (4 strings).

steps.title: Clean notes, no buzz
steps.body:
- Press with **fingertips**, just **behind** the fret (not on top of it, not in the middle).
- Keep the thumb behind the neck, roughly behind the middle finger.
- Arch fingers so they don't touch neighbouring strings.
- Short nails on the fretting hand.

steps.title: First strum pattern
steps.body:
In 4/4, count '1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &':

**D – D U – U D U** = Down on 1, (miss) on &, Down on 2, Up on &, (miss) on 3, Up on &, Down on 4, Up on &.

Keep the hand moving down-up all the time like a pendulum; just miss the strings on the silent strokes.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Practising 2 hours on day one — fingers blister. **15–20 minutes** daily is ideal at first.
- Waiting for a 'perfect' chord before changing; practise **changing** (Em ↔ Am, G ↔ C, D ↔ G) for one minute each.
- A guitar with very high strings (high 'action') is hard to play — a music shop can adjust it.

activity.prompt: Match each guitar string number to its note in standard tuning.

quiz.q: Standard tuning from thickest to thinnest is…
options: E B G D A E
A D G C E A
C G D A E B
E A D G B E
quiz.why: Standard guitar tuning from the thickest (lowest) string to the thinnest is E A D G B E.

quiz.q: Where should you press a string?
quiz.why: Press just behind the fret, not on top of it, to get a clean ringing note. Pressing in the middle of the space makes a dull or buzzing sound.

quiz.q: Which chord uses only two fingers on the 2nd fret?
quiz.why: E minor needs only two fingers, on the 2nd fret of the A and D strings. G and C use three fingers, and D uses three on different frets.

quiz.q: A good practice length for a beginner's first weeks is…
quiz.why: Fifteen to twenty minutes of practice daily lets fingertips adapt gradually. Long sessions or practising once a week are less effective.

quiz.q: How many strings do you strum for a D chord?
quiz.why: A D chord is strummed from the D string, so only 4 strings are played. The two lower strings are left out.

lessons.title: Keyboard: posture, fingering and the C major scale

scenes.text: Savitri, 66, in Mysuru, always wanted to play the keyboard. Her granddaughter buys her a 61-key keyboard.
Her teacher numbers her fingers 1 to 5 — thumb is 1 — and teaches her to tuck the thumb under for the C scale.
She practises 10 minutes after her morning walk.
On her granddaughter's birthday, she plays 'Happy Birthday' with both hands.

steps.title: Posture
steps.body:
- Sit at the centre of the keyboard (middle C in front of you).
- Forearms roughly **level** with the keys; elbows slightly in front of the body.
- Fingers **curved** as if holding a ball; play on the fingertips.
- Wrists relaxed — not collapsed, not raised high.

steps.title: Finger numbers
steps.body: Both hands: **thumb = 1, index = 2, middle = 3, ring = 4, little = 5**. Sheet music for beginners prints these numbers above notes.

steps.title: C major scale fingering (one octave)
steps.body:
**Right hand going up**: C(1) D(2) E(3) — **thumb tucks under** — F(1) G(2) A(3) B(4) C(5).
Coming down: C(5) B(4) A(3) G(2) F(1) — **3 crosses over** — E(3) D(2) C(1).

**Left hand going up**: C(5) D(4) E(3) F(2) G(1) — **3 crosses over** — A(3) B(2) C(1).
Coming down: C(1) B(2) A(3) — **thumb tucks under** — G(1) F(2) E(3) D(4) C(5).

steps.title: Practise slowly with a metronome
steps.body: Start around **60 BPM**, one note per click. When it is smooth 3 times in a row, raise it by 4–5 BPM. Hands separately first; then together.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Flat fingers — they slow you down and tire the hand.
- Lifting the elbow for the thumb tuck; keep the arm quiet and let the thumb move.
- Looking at the hands all the time — glance at the music; feel the two- and three-black-key groups.

activity.prompt: Order the right-hand C major scale going up with correct fingers.

quiz.q: Finger number 1 is the…
quiz.why: In piano fingering, the thumb is finger number 1 and the little finger is 5.

quiz.q: In the RH C major scale going up, the thumb tucks under after…
quiz.why: In the right-hand C major scale going up, the thumb tucks under after E, which is played with finger 3. The thumb then plays F.

quiz.q: Fingers on the keyboard should be…
quiz.why: Keep the fingers curved and play on the fingertips, as if holding a ball. Flat or stiff fingers are slow and tense.

quiz.q: When should you increase the metronome speed?
options: When it's smooth 3 times in a row
quiz.why: Increase the metronome speed only when you can play smoothly three times in a row. That way each new tempo is earned.

lessons.title: Tabla: bols, hand position and keherwa

scenes.text: Sameer, 13, in Lucknow, joins tabla classes. His 'Na' sounds like a dull thud.
Ustad-ji shows him: strike the edge (kinar) with the index finger and lift it immediately, while the ring finger rests lightly.
The next stroke rings like a bell.
In two months, Sameer plays keherwa theka steadily for the school assembly bhajan.

steps.title: The two drums
steps.body:
- **Dayan** (right-hand drum for right-handers): wooden, higher-pitched, tuned to the music's **Sa** (or sometimes Pa/Ma).
- **Bayan** (left-hand drum): usually metal or clay, lower and bass-heavy; its pitch can be bent by pressing with the wrist.
- Both have a black spot (**syahi**) made of layered paste that gives the tabla its ringing tone.

steps.title: Basic bols (strokes)
steps.body:
- **Na / Ta** (dayan): index finger strikes the outer edge (kinar), ring finger rests gently on the skin; lift the index quickly so it rings.
- **Tin** (dayan): index finger strikes the area between edge and syahi, ringing.
- **Tun** (dayan): index finger strikes the syahi with an open, ringing sound.
- **Ge / Ghe** (bayan): middle/index fingers strike the bayan's open area near the syahi, letting the bass ring.
- **Ke / Ka** (bayan): flat-hand closed stroke on the bayan — a short, dry sound.
- **Dha** = Na + Ge together. **Dhin** = Tin + Ge together.

Technique details differ a little between gharanas — follow your teacher.

steps.title: Keherwa theka (8 beats)
steps.body:
**Dha Ge Na Ti | Na Ka Dhi Na**

Clap on 1 (sam, X), wave on 5 (khali, 0). Play it slowly, counting aloud, until every stroke has the same volume. Then play it for 2 minutes without stopping.

steps.title: Posture and care
steps.body: Sit cross-legged (or on a low stool) with the drums on cloth rings, the dayan slightly tilted away. Keep wrists relaxed. Don't hit hard — tone comes from **quick, light strokes** that bounce off. Keep the drums away from moisture and direct sun.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Leaving the finger on the skin after Na — it kills the ring.
- Playing too loud and tense.
- Retuning with a hammer without guidance — ask your teacher first; the straps and blocks need care.

items.back: Dayan: index finger strikes the edge and lifts; ring finger rests lightly. Ringing.
Dayan: index finger between edge and syahi. Ringing.
Bayan: open bass stroke near the syahi, let it ring.
Bayan: flat-hand closed stroke, dry sound.
Na (dayan) + Ge (bayan) together.
Tin (dayan) + Ge (bayan) together.

quiz.q: The dayan is usually tuned to…
quiz.why: The dayan, the right-hand tabla drum, is usually tuned to the Sa of the music so it matches the other instruments.

quiz.q: Dha is a combination of…
quiz.why: Dha is a combined stroke of Na on the dayan and Ge on the bayan, played together.

quiz.q: To make Na ring, you should…
options: Strike the edge and lift the index quickly
quiz.why: For Na, strike the edge and lift the index finger quickly so the skin can ring. Pressing and holding damps the sound.

quiz.q: Keherwa theka is…
options: Dha Ge Na Ti | Na Ka Dhi Na
Dha Dhi Na | Dha Ti Na
quiz.why: Keherwa is an 8-beat theka: Dha Ge Na Ti | Na Ka Dhi Na. The other patterns belong to different taals.

quiz.q: Ke/Ka is a ___ stroke on the bayan.
quiz.why: Ke or Ka is a closed, dry stroke on the bayan made with a flat hand. Ringing strokes use the wrist and let the skin vibrate.

lessons.title: Bansuri: first tone and first notes

scenes.text: Gopal, 16, in Mathura, buys a bansuri at a fair. He blows hard — nothing but air.
A flute player at the ghat shows him: lips relaxed, a narrow stream of air across the hole, like blowing gently over a bottle top.
After 10 minutes, he gets a soft, hooting tone.
Within a month, Gopal plays Sa Re Ga Ma Pa every morning by the river.

steps.title: The bansuri
steps.body: The bansuri is a **side-blown bamboo flute** used in Hindustani classical, folk and film music. The common type has **six finger holes** plus the blowing hole (embouchure hole). Flutes come in many sizes; a **medium-sized flute** is a typical starter. Bigger flutes are lower and need wider finger stretches.

steps.title: Making the first tone
steps.body:
1. Hold the flute horizontally, usually extending to your right.
2. Rest the blowing hole against your lower lip, centred.
3. Lips relaxed, make a small opening as if saying 'pu'.
4. Blow a **gentle, focused** stream **across** the hole (not into it), aiming at the far edge.
5. Roll the flute slightly in or out until a tone appears.

It often takes a few practice sessions — this is normal.

steps.title: Fingering: Sa Re Ga
steps.body:
One hand covers the **top three holes** (nearest the blowing hole), the other covers the **bottom three**. Use the **pads** of the fingers, not the tips.

On a typical six-hole bansuri:

- **Sa** = top three holes closed, bottom three open.
- **Re** = top two closed.
- **Ga** = top one closed.
- **Lower Pa** = all six closed.

(Check with a tuner and your teacher's chart — flutes vary.)

steps.title: Breath and practice
steps.body: Practise **long notes**: hold Sa for 8 seconds, steady and clear. Then Re, Ga. Rest when you feel light-headed — over-blowing can make you dizzy. Practise 10–15 minutes daily.

steps.title: Common mistakes
steps.body:
- Blowing too hard (breathy, squeaky sound).
- Not fully sealing holes — even a small leak spoils the note.
- Lips too tight.
- Storing the flute in a hot car or wet place; bamboo can crack.

a.text: You've been trying for 15 minutes and the bansuri only makes air sounds. You feel frustrated.

choices.label: Blow harder
choices.feedback: Usually makes it worse.

choices.label: Relax lips, blow gently across the hole and roll the flute slightly
choices.feedback: This is the usual fix.

b.text: It squeaks and you feel dizzy.

choices.label: Rest a minute, then try gentle air and small adjustments
choices.feedback: Good — dizziness means you over-blew.

c.text: A soft tone appears, then disappears.

choices.label: Note the position and repeat it 10 times
choices.feedback: Repetition builds muscle memory.

choices.label: Give up — it's too hard
choices.feedback: Almost everyone struggles at first; stick with it a few more days.

end1.text: You found your embouchure! Next: long notes on Sa, Re, Ga.

end2.text: Take a break and come back tomorrow. Most beginners get a steady tone within a few days of practice.

quiz.q: The bansuri is…
quiz.why: The bansuri is a side-blown bamboo flute. It is not a metal flute, reed instrument or string instrument.

quiz.q: On a typical six-hole bansuri, Sa is played with…
quiz.why: On a typical six-hole bansuri, covering the top three holes while the bottom three are open gives Sa. All six closed gives the lower Pa.

quiz.q: Air should be directed…
options: Gently across the hole to its far edge
quiz.why: Direct the air gently across the blowing hole towards its far edge. Blowing straight into the hole or hard makes no clear tone.

quiz.q: Feeling dizzy while practising means…
quiz.why: Dizziness while playing a flute means you're over-blowing, so rest and use gentler air. It isn't a sign of doing great.

quiz.q: Finger holes should be covered with…
quiz.why: Cover the holes with the finger pads, the fleshy part, as they seal the holes better. Fingertips leave gaps and cause air leaks.

lessons.title: Practice that works: a 4-week starter plan for any instrument

scenes.text: Leela, 38, an accountant in Kolkata, starts keyboard but practises only when she 'feels like it' — and stops improving.
Her teacher gives her a simple structure: warm-up, technique, piece, fun — 20 minutes, 5 days a week, with a diary.
Each session has one tiny goal, like 'bars 5–8 at 70 BPM with no mistakes'.
Four weeks later she plays her first full piece for her family.

steps.title: The 20-minute session
steps.body:
- **3 min** – warm-up (scales, long notes, or slow theka).
- **5 min** – technique (one specific skill: chord changes, thumb-under, Na stroke, long tones).
- **8 min** – your piece or song: work on the **hardest few bars** first, slowly.
- **4 min** – fun: play something you already love, or improvise.

End by writing one line in your diary.

steps.title: Deliberate practice
steps.body:
- Set **one tiny goal** per session (specific and measurable).
- Slow down until you can play it **correctly**; then speed up a little.
- Repeat correct versions — practising mistakes teaches mistakes.
- Record yourself once a week and listen like a teacher.

steps.title: 4-week starter path
steps.body:
- **Week 1**: posture, first sounds, 2–3 notes or chords.
- **Week 2**: a scale or theka; first simple tune.
- **Week 3**: two tunes; start playing with a metronome or drone.
- **Week 4**: play one piece start to finish for someone; choose your next goal (a teacher, a graded exam syllabus, or a song list).

steps.title: Avoid strain
steps.body: Take a short break every 20–30 minutes. Stop if you feel pain (not just tiredness) in wrists, fingers, neck or back. Persistent pain, tingling or numbness should be checked by a doctor or physiotherapist.

activity.prompt: Set up your first practice week
items: Choose a fixed daily time (even 15–20 minutes)
Prepare a tuner, metronome or drone app
Write one tiny goal for tomorrow's session
Practise the hardest bars slowly first
Record yourself at the end of the week
Write one line in a practice diary after each session

quiz.q: In a short practice session, which part should usually get the most time?
options: Working slowly on the hardest bars of your piece
quiz.why: In a short session the most time should go to slow, focused work on the hardest bars, since that's where progress happens. Playing only what you already know adds little.

quiz.q: A good session goal is…
quiz.why: A good goal is specific and measurable, like 'bars 5–8 at 70 BPM with no mistakes'. Vague goals like 'get better' can't be checked.

quiz.q: Why slow down when making mistakes?
options: Repeating correct versions builds the right habit
quiz.why: Slow down when you make mistakes because you learn what you repeat. Repeating correct versions builds the right habit.

quiz.q: Tingling or numbness in your fingers that doesn't go away should be…
options: Checked by a doctor or physiotherapist
quiz.why: Tingling or numbness that won't go away may signal nerve or tendon trouble, so see a doctor or physiotherapist. Practising more may worsen it.

questions.q: Guitar standard tuning low to high is…
options: C F B E A D
E A D G C E
E A D G B E
D A D G A D
questions.why: Standard guitar tuning, from the lowest string to the highest, is E A D G B E.

questions.q: Thumb is finger number…
questions.why: In fingering, the thumb is number 1, and the fingers go 2 to 5 up to the little finger.

questions.q: The right-hand tabla drum (for right-handers) is the…
questions.why: The right-hand drum of the tabla, for right-handers, is the dayan. The left-hand drum is the bayan.

questions.q: The bansuri is made of…
questions.why: The bansuri is traditionally made of bamboo, which gives its sweet, breathy tone.

questions.q: Which chord strums only 4 strings?
questions.why: A D chord is played from the D string, so you strum only 4 strings. G, Em and C use five or six strings.

questions.q: Keherwa has how many beats?
questions.why: Keherwa has 8 beats, in two groups of four.

questions.q: RH C scale going up: the thumb plays which note after E?
questions.why: In the right-hand C major scale, after E (finger 3) the thumb tucks under and plays F. This lets the hand move up the keyboard smoothly.

questions.q: Dhin = ?
questions.why: Dhin is made from Tin on the dayan plus Ge on the bayan. Dha uses Na with Ge.

questions.q: Guitar notes buzz. Most likely fix?
options: Press just behind the fret with fingertips
questions.why: Buzzing usually means the finger is not just behind the fret or not pressing firmly. Use the fingertips close behind the fret.

questions.q: On a typical six-hole bansuri, all six holes closed gives…
questions.why: On a typical six-hole bansuri, closing all six holes gives the lower (mandra) Pa. Sa is played with only the top three closed.

questions.q: LH C scale going up: which finger crosses over after G (finger 1)?
questions.why: In the left-hand C scale going up, after G (finger 1) finger 3 crosses over the thumb to play A.

questions.q: Why does a tabla Na need the finger lifted instantly?
options: To let the skin ring freely
questions.why: Na needs the finger lifted instantly so the skin can ring freely. If the finger stays down it damps the sound.

questions.q: A beginner's best weekly plan?
options: Short daily sessions with slow, accurate repetition and a tiny goal
questions.why: Short daily sessions with slow, accurate repetition and a tiny goal build skill best. One long weekend session or fast playing makes mistakes into habits.
